key_insight: T2D-Bench tests whether LLM answers for type 2 diabetes are not just fluent, but also backed by explicit, graph-checkable evidence.
clinical_relevance: The framework could help surface unsupported or unsafe diabetes guidance, especially around medication safety and lifestyle-related glycemic claims.
method: Built a multi-layer knowledge graph combining UMLS, DrugBank, SIDER, ADA guideline rules, and lifestyle-to-glycemia links
Evaluated 100 structured vignettes across diagnosis, medication safety, and adversarial lifestyle conflicts
Used evidence-path checks plus constrained revision to enforce benchmark-defined evidence requirements
evidence_signal: In the abstract, baseline outputs failed evidence-path checks in 35% of cases for GPT-4o-mini and 33% for GPT-4o across 100 vignettes.
watch_item: Because the benchmark depends on a specific knowledge graph and rule set, performance may not fully capture real-world clinical nuance or all valid alternative recommendations.
paper_title: T2D-Bench: Evidence-Gated Evaluation of LLM Outputs for Type 2 Diabetes Using a Multi-Layer Clinical-Lifestyle Knowledge Graph
